elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Renewal remains automatic ("will renew automatically for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term"), and the conditional automatic-renewal elements below are not all satisfied (renewal term is not capped at 12 months, opt-out is 60 not 30 days, and there is no Vendor reminder), so the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Renewal is "for an additional term equal in duration to the previous term of the applicable Service Option Attachment" — an Order Form/Service Option Attachment with a term longer than 12 months rolls forward at that same length. No 12-month cap was inserted.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered text requires notice "at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term"; 60 > 30.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No renewal-reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered § 3.2 or § 4.1 language; the drafter acknowledges this in the rationale but did not add it.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the cited pricing provision states only that "Charges for applicable Services will be specified in Service Option Attachments and Order Forms" and may be one-time, installment, recurring or usage-based; no renewal uplift or price-adjustment mechanic is granted, so there is no increase to cap.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 3.2 now reads "unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — a 60-day window, exactly at the fallback ceiling. The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a false negative caused by the spelled-out/parenthetical numeral form; the substantive figure is 60.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: charges are fixed by the Service Option Attachments and Order Forms and the Agreement contains no renewal-price-increase right, so no 5 percent cap is required.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single word change from "ninety (90)" to "sixty (60)" brings the non-renewal notice window to exactly 60 days, and the price-cap element is vacuously satisfied because no renewal uplift right exists in the Agreement.

Preferred level is not complete — three defects would need operative repair: (a) cap each renewal term at twelve (12) months rather than "a term equal in duration to the previous term"; (b) reduce Customer's opt-out to thirty (30) days; (c) add an express Vendor obligation to notify Customer at least sixty (60) days before each automatic renewal. Classifying the finding as a deviation and curing only to the fallback is consistent with the playbook, which does not redline preferred-only sub-elements.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only the numeral that drives the selected fallback element, leaves the mutual notice structure, the roll-forward term language, and the § 4.1 charges sentence untouched, and adds no extra procedure, reminder, or uplift cap outside the fallback checklist.

Intent is preserved: the clause remains a symmetrical either-party non-renewal mechanic tied to the end of the then-current term, with no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence. Note the collateral effect that Vendor's own non-renewal notice also drops from 90 to 60 days, giving us less advance warning; that is inherent in the mutual drafting and a party-specific split would be a larger edit, but flag it to the deal team.

Residual risk to monitor (not a checklist failure): because renewal duration tracks the previous term, a multi-year Order Form would produce an automatic multi-year renewal, which is walk-away territory under this rule. If any Service Option Attachment has a term over 12 months, escalate rather than accept the fallback.
Correct the deterministic notice-window check to recognise spelled-number-plus-parenthetical forms ("sixty (60)"); as run it produced a false negative that contradicts the rendered text.
